recent_posts.title: Atlassian launches AI-native service management platform with agentic workflows
recent_posts.summary: Atlassian is announcing its 'Service Collection' platform, positioning it as an AI-native replacement for traditional service desk tools. Key features include Rovo Service for autonomous multi-step workflow execution (available now), an Incident Command Center consolidating alerting and investigation with AI-driven root cause analysis (coming soon), and Solution Composer for generating service workflows from natural language descriptions (coming soon). The platform is built around the 'Teamwork Graph' data layer that connects people, tools, issues, and knowledge to provide context for AI models. The vision is proactive, invisible service that resolves issues before users notice them, with AI agents working alongside humans.

recent_posts.title: Our Q3 FY26 letter to shareholders
recent_posts.summary: Atlassian's Q3 FY26 shareholder letter reports $1.8B total revenue (up 32% y/y) and cloud revenue exceeding $1.1B (up 29% y/y). Service Collection surpassed $1B ARR growing over 30% y/y, with 65,000+ customers including over half the Fortune 500. Rovo AI customers are growing ARR at 2x the rate of non-Rovo customers, with AI credit usage growing 20%+ month-over-month. Key highlights include record competitive displacements from legacy ITSM providers, the general availability of Rovo Service (an AI agent for employee support), and the launch of Proactive AIOps. Teamwork Collection customers use 2x more AI credits per user and have 2x more active agents versus standalone customers. RPO grew to $4B (up 37% y/y).

recent_posts.title: Designing In Variables: How Control Panels Accelerate The Way We Design
recent_posts.summary: A designer at Atlassian shares how using control panels in AI prototypes has transformed their workflow. Control panels are lightweight interfaces embedded in prototypes with toggles, sliders, and dropdowns that let designers switch between states and variables in real time. This approach replaces managing multiple static files with a single living prototype, enabling faster exploration of tradeoffs, earlier stakeholder involvement, and clearer communication with engineers and product managers. The post covers practical use cases, prompt examples for building control panels with AI agents, and future directions including canvas orchestration and feeding prototype discoveries back into the Atlassian Design System.

recent_posts.title: Designing AI products you can depend on
recent_posts.summary: Building AI products that earn trust requires treating AI as a design material rather than a feature. Key principles include exposing intent before output, surfacing uncertainty signals, designing for human participation, and decomposing outputs into stages. Drawing from experience building AI features in Jira Service Management, the author argues that dependability comes from deliberate design choices—checkpoints, confidence signals, correction paths—not just model quality. Content design shapes AI behavior through system prompts, and evaluation metrics should focus on output structure, tone consistency, verbosity, and correction cost rather than just latency and accuracy.

recent_posts.title: New grads are your fastest path to AI adoption and companies are cutting them
recent_posts.summary: Atlassian's Teamwork Lab research finds that new graduates (ages 21–24) are 1.5x more likely to be daily AI users and 1.7x more likely to treat AI as a creative partner compared to older tech workers. Inside Atlassian, engineering new grads are 19% more likely to be AI superusers and 1.8x as likely to spend an hour or more daily experimenting with AI. The research argues that companies cutting early-career hiring to save costs are inadvertently stalling their AI adoption momentum. A notable finding: younger workers are 38% more likely to hide their AI use from managers due to unclear policies and cultural stigma, which prevents team-wide learning. Recommendations include setting clear AI working agreements, leading by example, and building early-career pipelines that treat new grads as strategic AI collaborators.

recent_posts.title: Inside Atlassian’s Merge Queues: How we ship faster with fewer incidents
recent_posts.summary: Atlassian shares how adopting Bitbucket Merge Queues across 70+ large repositories (Jira, Rovo, Trello) reduced semantic merge conflict failures from 7–10% to nearly zero and cut weekly merge-related incidents from 3–5 to rare edge cases. The system validates each queued PR against the expected future state of the target branch before merging, eliminating the need for manual coordination and quiet-window strategies. The Jira team configured queues with 14 concurrent builds and parallel parent-child pipelines, resulting in build times dropping from 40 to 35 minutes and developer satisfaction rising from 70% to 82%.

recent_posts.title: Why marketers should use AI on real problems instead of dedicated experimentation sprints
recent_posts.summary: Most marketing teams treat AI adoption as a separate experimentation sprint, resulting in prompt libraries and tool comparisons but zero changed workflows. The core argument is that AI delivers real value only when applied to live, in-context problems rather than hypothetical scenarios. Instead of blocking time for open-ended AI exploration, marketers should build a 10–15% buffer into project timelines and reach for AI when genuinely stuck. Connected systems that carry existing context (briefs, data, past campaigns) outperform blank-slate chat windows. Marketing Ops is identified as the ideal internal champion because of their end-to-end system visibility. Practical examples include using AI to complete half-baked briefs, draft quarterly report narratives, and unblock stalled approval chains. The recommended approach mirrors campaign optimization: try, measure, iterate, and scale what works organically.

recent_posts.title: Forrester on Getting AI-Ready & Modernizing Workplaces
recent_posts.summary: A commissioned Forrester Consulting study of 280 global IT leaders reveals that team silos and tool fragmentation are the top barriers to AI adoption in enterprises. Key findings: 68% of C-level IT executives cite silos as their biggest challenge, 82% rely on two or more vendors for work management, and only 14% have achieved enterprise-wide AI operationalization. The study advocates for consolidating onto fewer, more extensible platforms with stronger governance as the foundation for scaling AI across organizations.

recent_posts.title: Beyond the Jira board: how autonomous workflows unlock engineering velocity
recent_posts.summary: Engineers spend only 16% of their time writing code, with the remaining 84% on coordination, documentation, and context-gathering. Atlassian's Teamwork Collection (Jira, Confluence, Loom, and Rovo AI) aims to reduce this friction through a connected data model called the Teamwork Graph. Key capabilities include Loom-powered async communication that auto-generates Jira tickets and Confluence pages, Rovo AI agents that handle triage, bug analysis, and documentation tasks, and integration with third-party agents like GitHub Copilot. Reported outcomes include 80% of new-hire questions answered by Rovo agents at Sprout Social, 75% reduction in roadmap writing time at Procore, and 100+ hours saved per engineer annually at Atlassian.

recent_posts.title: Design Technologists: The role that turns creativity into code
recent_posts.summary: Atlassian introduces the Design Technologist (DT) role, which bridges design and engineering by building interactive, data-connected prototypes that enable faster decision-making. DTs think like designers but code like engineers, integrating AI into design-system scaffolding to let teams create realistic prototypes quickly. Internal metrics show 35% month-over-month growth in AI prototyping activity, 92% of PMs and designers reporting improved decision-making, over 12,000 AI-powered prototypes running across teams, and 42% of the design team reporting faster delivery speeds.

top_posts.title: Bitbucket’s new look: user experience and navigation updates coming soon
top_posts.summary: Bitbucket Cloud is getting a visual redesign and navigation overhaul in early 2026, aligning with Atlassian's unified design system. The update includes modernized navigation for faster access to repositories, pull requests, and pipelines, along with improved typography, color system, iconography, and components for better readability and accessibility. Icons and components will roll out progressively over the coming weeks, with the full navigation update launching early next year.

top_posts.title: Software documentation tools for developers in 2025
top_posts.summary: Software documentation tools help developers and teams share knowledge effectively across code, APIs, projects, and end-users. The article categorizes documentation into four types (developer, project, marketing/sales, and end-user) and reviews eight tools across different categories: code documentation (GitHub, Confluence, Jira), API documentation (Swagger UI, Document360), help authoring (Adobe RoboHelp, MadCap Flare), and video collaboration (Loom). Key evaluation criteria include rich-text editing, version control, organization features, collaboration capabilities, templates, integrations, and security. Each tool is assessed with features, pros, cons, and pricing information.

top_posts.title: Behind the screens: Building Atlassian’s new icon system
top_posts.summary: Atlassian redesigned their entire icon system after six years, moving from 350+ inconsistent icons to a unified system with thinner strokes, consistent sizing, and better visual harmony. The project included building Icon Lab for team contributions, creating automated migration tools, and establishing clear naming conventions. Over 275 new icons have been contributed, with migration tools handling 16,000+ code changes across their products.

top_posts.title: Confluence vs. Notion: Find the right fit for your business
top_posts.summary: Confluence and Notion are content creation and collaboration platforms with different strengths. Confluence is designed for enterprise organizations with large teams and complex workflows, while Notion is targeted towards individuals and personal use. Confluence offers extensive integrations and admin controls, while Notion has a simpler interface. The pricing for Confluence ranges from a free plan to enterprise plans based on the number of users.

top_posts.title: Atlassian Marketplace now supports single install across Jira and Confluence
top_posts.summary: Atlassian Marketplace now supports multi-app compatibility, allowing a single app to work across both Jira and Confluence without separate installations. Admins install an app once into its primary host (the 'Requires' app) and can then connect it to additional Atlassian apps via the Admin hub at no extra cost. Billing is tied to the seat count of the primary installation context. Over 20 apps are already available with this capability, including HR, reporting, and dashboard tools.
